newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Mobil Sekiyu's profits fall 10.2 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Japan Mobil Sekiyu's profits fall 10.2 pct in 1996.

text.p: Mobil Sekiyu KK, a subsidiary of U.S. oil major Mobil Corp, said on Tuesday its current profits in 1996 fell 10.2 percent from the previous year, marking a decline for the second year running.
The oil product wholesaler's current profits in 1996 amounted to 7.71 billion yen, down 874 million yen from 8.58 billion yen in 1995.
The fall came in spite of growth in sales of oil products, which increased by 5.8 percent from the previous year to 17.6 million kilolitres, Mobil Sekiyu said.
Profits slipped on weak gasoline retail prices, which fell despite a surge in yen-based costs to procure crude oil, Mobil Sekiyu director Tsuneo Ogawa told reporters.
Yen-denominated costs were pulled up by higher global crude prices combined with a weaker yen against the dollar.
The outlook for 1997 remains bleak, Ogawa said.
"With sentiment in the economy failing to improve whatsoever and deregulation in the oil industry taking its toll, an even more severe era awaits oil firms," Ogawa said.
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities such as investment in stocks.
